title: Keys and letters: The Final Countdown

blocks.text:
This course teaches the same skills as the step-by-step course, in the same order, but every skill comes from a song: the riff you practise is the riff from the record.

**By the end** of this lesson you can name any white key on the piano and play the riff of *The Final Countdown* by its key names.

blocks.caption: The Final Countdown, the opening riff (a PDMX lead sheet). ▶ to hear it and watch the keys.

blocks.text:
# The map: groups of black keys
The black keys come in groups: two together, then three together, over and over up the keyboard. They are your map. Every white key is named from where it sits next to a group.

The white keys are named with the first seven letters, **A B C D E F G**, going up (to the right), then starting again at A. **C** is the white key just left of a group of two. **F** is just left of a group of three. **A** is between the upper two keys of a group of three.

blocks.alt: A keyboard with the groups of two and three black keys outlined
blocks.caption: Groups of two and three black keys: C sits left of each two, F left of each three.

blocks.title: Find each key by its letter
blocks.about: Twelve cards: a letter comes up, you find it.

blocks.text:
# The riff
The riff uses six white keys, from A up to F: A B C D E F. Put your right thumb on the A above the middle of the keyboard (the A between the upper two black keys of a group of three) and let one finger rest on each key up to E. F is one key past your little finger: reach up to it with finger 5 and come back.

blocks.notes: A4 B4 C5 D5 E5 F5
blocks.caption: The riff's six keys: thumb on A, finger 5 on E, and finger 5 reaching up to F.

blocks.text: Its notes, in order: **E D E A**, then **F E F E D**, **E D E A**, then **D C D C B D**. The riff is said in pairs: a fast little turn, then a long note. On the cards the letters come up one phrase at a time; play each when you've read it. Hear it plays the card for you if you're stuck.

blocks.title: The riff by its key names
blocks.about: Two phrases of letters; Hear it if you're stuck.

blocks.text:
# Another riff: Seven Nation Army
The White Stripes' riff, in your left hand: **E E G E D C B**. Its first note is the E below middle C. In Wait for me the music waits for each key.

# If this happens
- **You can't find A.** Find a group of three black keys; A is the white key between its upper two.
- **You play D for E.** E is just right of a group of two, D in the middle of it.

**Until the next lesson:** the riff by names once a day, and the find-a-key cards for a minute.
